notes: §1985:XI.4.1.4 GR8 defines the output procedure's range dynamically (statements reached by CALL, EXIT, GO TO and PERFORM, and declaratives run from it) and says only that 'The range of the output procedure must not cause the execution of any MERGE, RELEASE, or SORT statement', a run-time prohibition with no stated result; §1985:XI.4.4.3 SR1 places a SORT 'anywhere in the Procedure Division except in the declarative portion'. EmitMerge runs the output procedure as a performed range, so paragraphs PERFORMed from it outside its sections belong to it, and since kb/Work PB5274 GateSortMergeProcedures reports the lexical SORT ban (COBOL2700) and the MERGE ban (COBOL1572) only at 2023, so a 1985 program that writes them in the procedure without executing them compiles. Probes at --std 85 (classes b, c, e): g8a, a SORT and a MERGE written under a false IF in the output procedure, compiles and prints AAA BBB CCC DONE (at --std 2023 COBOL2700 and COBOL1572); g8b, the same SORT executed, ends the run with I-O status 41 on IN1 (undefined in 1985, the violation is the program's); g8c, a RELEASE PERFORMed from the output procedure, is refused COBOL7081 under §1985:XI.4.2.3 SR2, a neighbouring rule. Classes a, d and f do not reach the range rule. The witness RETURNs through GET-REC in another section and prints AAA BBB CCC DDD DONE. History: until the 1985 re-read 5 (2026-11-14) this row read DIVERGES, naming kb/Work PB5274 (landed); the re-read of main dc1f2dcce8 found that defect fixed by the landing of kb/Work PB5274 and records CONFORMS, upheld by an independent refuter (code read: op-20261114/out-reread5/rs-12.json, refuter op-20261114/out-reread5/rs-12-refute.json).

next.reason: The range definition is kept (2023 says any 'transfer of control' rather than listing CALL, EXIT, GO TO, PERFORM) and so is the ban. 1985 'must not' states no result; 2023 says 'If this rule is violated, the EC-SORT-MERGE-ACTIVE exception condition is set to exist and the results of the merge operation are undefined' (§2023:14.9.24.4 GR8), and a RELEASE there also sets EC-FLOW-RELEASE (§2023:14.9.32.4 GR1). 2023 also refuses at compile time a MERGE written 'in an output procedure of another MERGE statement' (§2023:14.9.24.3 SR1) and a SORT written 'in an input or output procedure' (§2023:14.9.40.3 SR3); 1985 SR1 allowed both anywhere outside declaratives. Limiting the ban to 'the file format of the SORT statement' only exempts the new table SORT.
